top_choice_rationale: P002 recognises a physical-chemical design rule for ionizable lipids and their self-assembly: a pKa tuned near 6 to 7 keeps the particle near-neutral in blood and cationic in the acidifying endosome, where ion pairing with anionic lipids drives a non-bilayer phase transition that releases the cargo. It is independently validated at scale and complementary to the 2023 Medicine prize for the cargo. Cullis, MacLachlan and Anderson cover the pKa-tuned lipid and the combinatorial route to new lipids. Attribution is the weak point (Hope, Madden, Langer), but that is a choice among deserving people, not doubt about the science. P001 is mature and cleanly attributed to Buchwald and Hartwig, but it extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize to a new bond, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my lipid self-assembly and membrane research overlaps thematically with P002, but I have no apparent personal or collaborative tie to the proposed laureates
